market_reason: A global bond rout has pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level since 2002 and European stocks to three-month lows. The move is significant but widely reported, and equities are down only modestly.
market_headlines: U.S. Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002 - The New York Times
European stocks close at three-month lows as surging bond yields hammer banks - Reuters
Stock Market Midday, Oct. 1: Stocks Edge Lower as Treasury Yields Surge to 24-Year High - Yahoo Finance
summary: Surging Treasury yields (24-year high), rate-hike expectations and a global bond sell-off are pressuring equities, which matters most for the leveraged Nasdaq position (QLD). China's fuel export suspension is lifting oil, which helps the energy and commodity holdings, and no ETF-specific shock calls for a veto.
